chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Basie's arrangers: Mundy, Gibson, Clayton, Dameron
summary: Tate lists those who wrote for the band, including Buster Harding's boogies and Skip Martin.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: By this time, did Basie have arrangers, staff arrangers?

Yeah, yeah, he did. Of course, he would -- he'd listen to anybody's arrangement, you know, but Jimmy Mundy did a lot of writing for the band, and Andy Gibson -- I don't think Andy -- yeah, Andy did a lot of writing for the band and Buck used to do a lot.

Tadd did, Tad did quite a few things. And Buster Harding used to write all the boogies, you know, like for Basie. He did the piano boogies. Buster Harding did that. He bought arrangements from everybody -- Skip Martin, Skip, I think, wrote "Miss Thing." Skip is a white saxophone player. Dave Matthews wrote some things for him. I don't know what became of Dave, that's my Texas friend. And just about everybody.
